supports typed verification cases, evidence requirements, provider/method eligibility, route coverage, integer-cent costing, and bounded optimization across combinations of verification routes. Travel is charged once for a shared visit by the same provider.\n\nThe new planner was tested with both a Houston ITAD equipment scenario and a Dallas property scenario. Its tests confirm that\\:\n\n- Seller photos cannot satisfy a working-condition check, and a generic web lookup cannot satisfy a title-verification requirement.\n- Estimated or conditional partner costs cannot masquerade as documented, available quotes.\n- Shared site visits reduce costs without incorrectly combining different providers.\n- A plan that exceeds budget or lacks necessary verification remains incomplete.\n- Planning never dispatches an inspector, admits evidence, or authorizes expenditure.\n\nThis is a native extension of the existing Economy owner—not a new JSON document store. None of these counts a guide, README, architecture diagram, documentation refresh, or standalone dashboard as a demo.\n\nFor a maturity to count as delivered, a visitor must be able to bring in or select a meaningful source, change something, see its consequences, save or continue the work, and reach an actual output or authorized downstream operation. The resulting application also needs a second representative scenario, negative-path testing, and a verified browser experience.\n\n### A. Mature the current Aurekai experiences — 8\n\n| # | Product-level maturity | What the finished user journey must do |\n|---|---|---|\n| **01** | **Retail Space → Procurement Studio** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Existing RED3 planner</text> | Plan multiple spaces and layouts, import sourced fixtures, enforce dimensions and clearance constraints, compare configurations and landed costs, request supplier verification, prepare a reviewed RFQ, then track procurement and installation work. Preserve the current planner’s save/share/review flow. |\n| **02** | **Multi-Merchant Catalogue Operations** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Existing product editor</text> | Import and reconcile whole catalogues rather than editing one product. Manage variant identity, stock, images, source-price changes, localization, SEO and channel mappings; approve grouped changes; apply through authorized merchant adapters; verify receiving-store results and rollback. |\n| **03** | **Shipment-to-Books Operations** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Shipment reconciliation example</text> | Accept mixed documents, scans and manifests; identify the shipment, correlate carrier and delivery evidence, recover exceptions, compute service/cost obligations and prepare accounting handoffs. Publish changes only through the site's authorized owner. |\n| **05** | **Native Creator Audio Studio** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Live audio mixer</text> | Graduate from three generated tones to uploaded multitrack material: waveform/timeline editing, clips, automation, native C/Wasm mixing, bounded streaming, quality comparison, export variants, provenance, rights review and release preparation. |\n| **06** | **Interactive Studio & Member Operations** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Existing local training app</text> | Bring the already-built coach/member application into a hosted, safe multi-role sandbox. Complete enrolment, programming, calendar/device import, offline training, performance history, coach review, versioned publication and governed membership/finance handoffs. |\n| **07** | **Research & Knowledge Operations** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Existing local document workspace</text> | Turn local cited search into a full source-to-research workbench: batch imports, recording/media passages, comparison across sources, persistent annotations, reusable research collections, exceptions, cited findings and downstream WorkGraph handoffs. |\n| **08** | **Multi-Business Merchant Operating System** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Three live branded businesses</text> | Operate Fernhollow, Tallgrass and Juniper through one underlying system while keeping tenants isolated. Staff must be able to claim work, resolve conflicts, acknowledge a handoff and carry an incident through recovery and retrospective learning. |\n| **11** | **Grant Funding & Impact Operations** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Grant Evidence</text> | Gather program material, test eligibility, assemble an application, define approved budgets and milestones, match spending to deliverables, support human review and produce funder-ready progress/impact reports. |\n| **12** | **Procurement Memory & Negotiation Room** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Procurement Memory</text> | Import contracts, RFPs, vendor calls and purchase histories; extract obligations and deadlines; compare competing offers; run a controlled negotiation and approval path; then track renewal, purchasing and delivery. |\n| **13** | **Town-in-a-Box Civic Operations** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Town Box</text> | Convert meeting records, resident issues and local service requests into a shared civic work program. Residents and officials see different authorized views, issues progress through responsible owners, and public updates connect back to the original source. |\n| **14** | **Oral History & Museum Experience Studio** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Museum Exhibit + Family History + Local Archive</text> | Ingest recordings, photos, documents and collections; curate interactive timelines, maps and exhibits; control identity/consent and corrections; create multilingual or audio experiences; and publish a navigable exhibition that retains source relationships. |\n| **15** | **Open-Source Maintainer & Release Workbench** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">OSS Cockpit + Explain Repo</text> | Connect a repository; inspect issues, changes, failed checks and documentation; reproduce a specific problem; prioritize work; draft and review a patch; and follow it through tests, release gates and documentation changes. |\n| **16** | **Revenue & Customer Intelligence Studio** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Sales Distiller + Customer Voice + Competitive Intel</text> | Combine customer conversations, objections, feedback, public competitor changes and CRM history. New experiences built from the existing native ecosystem — 14\n\n| # | New full application | End-to-end operating experience |\n|---|---|---|\n| **17** | **Configurable Acquisition Brief Studio** | The user selects a business/domain, imports candidate opportunities, composes their own decision criteria, sees source-linked evidence and economics, configures required verification, and previews different recipient-specific briefs. **2nd Life and Fleming** are initial domain configurations using the same native semantics, bindings and projection machinery—not stored JSON briefs. |\n| **18** | **ITAD Acquisition & Disposition Exchange** | Source off-market equipment, reconcile manifests and photos, identify hardware, model resale yield and logistics, secure seller/inspector verification, match equipment to buyer criteria, negotiate terms and track custody, collection, refurbishment and disposition. 2nd Life is the example buyer, without implying an engagement. |\n| **19** | **Fleming Estate-to-Exit Studio** | Build from Dallas property observations through owner/estate research, parcel relationships, tax/title exceptions, scenario underwriting, investor and builder matching, reviewed outreach, agreements and closing work. That work is not credited against the 30 demo maturities.\n\n**Current result:** 30 distinct, substantial programs identified and grounded in existing products or native capabilities. They are **not being misreported as 30 finished deployments**. The live-site, GitHub Pages, native-source and documentation inventories are now separated, and no additional ZIPs, runtime JSON schemas or duplicate demo repositories were created in this pass. Residents and officials see different authorized views, issues progress through responsible owners, and public updates connect back to the original source. |\n| **14** | **Oral History &amp; Museum Experience Studio** Museum Exhibit + Family History + Local Archive | Ingest recordings, photos, documents and collections; curate interactive timelines, maps and exhibits; control identity/consent and corrections; create multilingual or audio experiences; and publish a navigable exhibition that retains source relationships. |\n| **15** | **Open-Source Maintainer &amp; Release Workbench** OSS Cockpit + Explain Repo | Connect a repository; inspect issues, changes, failed checks and documentation; reproduce a specific problem; prioritize work; draft and review a patch; and follow it through tests, release gates and documentation changes. |\n| **16** | **Revenue &amp; Customer Intelligence Studio** Sales Distiller + Customer Voice + Competitive Intel | Combine customer conversations, objections, feedback, public competitor changes and CRM history. Use the compiled native application contracts, actual authorization and work transitions—not a gallery of DocTypes and field counts. |\n| **28** | **Institution ProcessTwin &amp; Intervention Foundry** | Ingest actual permitted event histories, reconstruct OCEL-style process paths and manual workarounds, identify bottlenecks or drift, simulate alternatives through admitted predictors/HVM2, and test approved interventions. Those boundaries should be preserved as the portfolio expands.\n\n## 30 full-demo-equivalent maturities\n\nThe audit resolves to **8 major maturities of existing Work Samples experiences, 8 major upgrades of existing GitHub Pages applications, and 14 new cross-system experiences**. None of these counts a guide, README, architecture diagram, documentation refresh, or standalone dashboard as a demo.\n\nFor a maturity to count as delivered, a visitor must be able to bring in or select a meaningful source, change something, see its consequences, save or continue the work, and reach an actual output or authorized downstream operation. The resulting application also needs a second representative scenario, negative-path testing, and a verified browser experience.\n\n### A. Mature the current Aurekai experiences — 8\n\n| # | Product-level maturity | What the finished user journey must do |\n|---|---|---|\n| **01** | **Retail Space → Procurement Studio** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Existing RED3 planner</text> | Plan multiple spaces and layouts, import sourced fixtures, enforce dimensions and clearance constraints, compare configurations and landed costs, request supplier verification, prepare a reviewed RFQ, then track procurement and installation work. Preserve the current planner’s save/share/review flow. |\n| **02** | **Multi-Merchant Catalogue Operations** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Existing product editor</text> | Import and reconcile whole catalogues rather than editing one product. Manage variant identity, stock, images, source-price changes, localization, SEO and channel mappings; approve grouped changes; apply through authorized merchant adapters; verify receiving-store results and rollback. |\n| **03** | **Shipment-to-Books Operations** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Shipment reconciliation example</text> | Accept mixed documents, scans and manifests; identify the shipment, correlate carrier and delivery evidence, recover exceptions, compute service/cost obligations and prepare accounting handoffs. A reviewer can resolve a real batch, not merely read an eight-file report. |\n| **04** | **Website Reconstruction & Conversion Laboratory** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Existing Wix review</text> | Use REA and ForeignTwin to inspect an actual site, reconstruct its page/link/content system, identify duplicate intent and broken journeys, model replacement pages and compare before/after outcomes. Publish changes only through the site's authorized owner. |\n| **05** | **Native Creator Audio Studio** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Live audio mixer</text> | Graduate from three generated tones to uploaded multitrack material: waveform/timeline editing, clips, automation, native C/Wasm mixing, bounded streaming, quality comparison, export variants, provenance, rights review and release preparation. |\n| **06** | **Interactive Studio & Member Operations** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Existing local training app</text> | Bring the already-built coach/member application into a hosted, safe multi-role sandbox. Complete enrolment, programming, calendar/device import, offline training, performance history, coach review, versioned publication and governed membership/finance handoffs. |\n| **07** | **Research & Knowledge Operations** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Existing local document workspace</text> | Turn local cited search into a full source-to-research workbench: batch imports, recording/media passages, comparison across sources, persistent annotations, reusable research collections, exceptions, cited findings and downstream WorkGraph handoffs. |\n| **08** | **Multi-Business Merchant Operating System** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Three live branded businesses</text> | Operate Fernhollow, Tallgrass and Juniper through one underlying system while keeping tenants isolated. Each has relevant offers, availability or enquiries, customer conversations, quotes, work fulfilment, invoices and a complete operator/customer journey. |\n\n### B. Promote existing GitHub Pages projects into substantial applications — 8\n\nThese are **maturities, not new repository proposals**. Their existing source and preview mechanisms should be reused rather than replaced by new islands.\n\n| # | Product-level maturity | What the finished user journey must do |\n|---|---|---|\n| **09** | **Podcast Production & Distribution Plant** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Podcast Plant</text> | Import or record an episode; edit its transcript and timeline; create clips, chapters, show notes and social variants; verify media/rights; preview everything; approve an RSS release; and inspect the published output. |\n| **10** | **Shift Handoff & Incident Continuity** <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Shift Handoff + Postmortem Atlas</text> | Turn spoken or written handoffs into owned tasks, priority decisions, incident histories and durable next-shift context. Turn them into actionable opportunities, reviewed follow-ups, source-linked product changes, and a pipeline that distinguishes proposal value from accepted revenue and collected cash. |\n\n### C. New experiences built from the existing native ecosystem — 14\n\n| # | New full application | End-to-end operating experience |\n|---|---|---|\n| **17** | **Configurable Acquisition Brief Studio** | The user selects a business/domain, imports candidate opportunities, composes their own decision criteria, sees source-linked evidence and economics, configures required verification, and previews different recipient-specific briefs. **2nd Life and Fleming** are initial domain configurations using the same native semantics, bindings and projection machinery—not stored JSON briefs. |\n| **18** | **ITAD Acquisition & Disposition Exchange** | Source off-market equipment, reconcile manifests and photos, identify hardware, model resale yield and logistics, secure seller/inspector verification, match equipment to buyer criteria, negotiate terms and track custody, collection, refurbishment and disposition. 2nd Life is the example buyer, without implying an engagement. |\n| **19** | **Fleming Estate-to-Exit Studio** | Build from Dallas property observations through owner/estate research, parcel relationships, tax/title exceptions, scenario underwriting, investor and builder matching, reviewed outreach, agreements and closing work. Bundle multiple checks into a single visit, account for travel and capacity, request actual quotes, dispatch only through approved authority and reconcile cost with completed evidence. |\n| **22** | **Universal ForeignTwin Import & Clip Studio** | Import one URL or thousands of source items from YouTube, Twitch, public meetings, news, RSS and other permitted providers. Discover native carriers, inspect retained material and rights, search or scrub a synchronized media timeline, make clips, create translations and project approved excerpts into other Aurekai experiences. |\n| **23** | **Dallas Civic Media & Agenda Studio** | Incrementally synchronize agenda records, meeting occurrences, chaptered recordings and related documents. Exact provider identities join the sources; users search, watch at the matched timestamp, annotate an item and follow downstream actions. Unmatched chapters remain reviewable rather than fabricated. This also provides a reusable municipal-media product. |\n| **24** | **SEAR Supply & Resource Scenario Operator** | Operate a simulated supply network with real constraint types: vendor capability, resource weather, inventory, location, transport, cost, shortage and disruption. Compare alternatives, reroute supply, test failure/recovery and hand an approved plan to the proper procurement/logistics owner—not pretend a synthetic optimum is a real purchase. |\n| **25** | **MHS Instrument & Research Operations Studio** | Discover typed instrument capabilities and facility requirements, schedule reservations, model contention and resource allocation, enforce qualifications/interlocks, and run digital experiments. Human-approved transitions can enter a separately admitted real-instrument path; the demo must visibly refuse unsafe or unavailable execution. |\n| **26** | **REA Software Twin Foundry** | Analyze a repository, site or supported desktop application; reconstruct relevant structure, state transitions, resource dependencies and interface behavior; generate a working sandbox twin; compare it with the source; and produce an inspectable extension, migration or replacement path with behavioral regression tests. |\n| **27** | **Frappe Enterprise Application Workbench** | Let someone operate a cross-application business: CRM opportunity → quote → ERPNext purchasing/inventory → Helpdesk fulfilment → invoice/finance, with Drive/Wiki material and HRMS roles. Use the compiled native application contracts, actual authorization and work transitions—not a gallery of DocTypes and field counts. |\n| **28** | **Institution ProcessTwin & Intervention Foundry** | Ingest actual permitted event histories, reconstruct OCEL-style process paths and manual workarounds, identify bottlenecks or drift, simulate alternatives through admitted predictors/HVM2, and test approved interventions. Compare projected vs observed outcomes, preserve recovery and explain why a candidate is or isn't deployable. |\n| **29** | **Protocol Commerce & Service Exchange** | Discover a real need or resource, match a capable provider, compare quoted terms, negotiate through supported commerce protocols (including x402/Beckn where admitted), obtain assent, check payment/entitlement, deliver the service and reconcile economic receipts. Unsupported settlement rails stay visibly unavailable rather than faked. |\n| **30** | **Community Projects, Funding & Voucher Studio** | A community proposes a project, establishes a governed decision process, recruits people and suppliers, prices work, coordinates funding commitments, issues bounded QR/voucher entitlements where supported, tracks delivery and publishes an accountable community outcome with appeal and correction paths. |\n\n## The common execution graph\n\nThese should not become 30 copies of the same standalone dashboard. They should be 30 different experiences supported by common native operations.\n\n<box border radius=\"lg\" padding={3} gap={2}>\n  <grid columns={2} gap={3}>\n    <grid-item>\n      <text weight=\"medium\">Discovery & intake</text>\n      <caption>ForeignTwin, external estate, content/source owners</caption>\n    </grid-item>\n    <grid-item>\n      <text weight=\"medium\">User-specific decisions</text>\n      <caption>Typed criteria, domain bindings, alternatives, provenance</caption>\n    </grid-item>\n    <grid-item>\n      <text weight=\"medium\">Actions & coordination</text>\n      <caption>WorkGraph, actors, leases, review and authorized transitions</caption>\n    </grid-item>\n    <grid-item>\n      <text weight=\"medium\">Economics & capacity</text>\n      <caption>Finance, provider selection, resource admission, real quotes</caption>\n    </grid-item>\n    <grid-item>\n      <text weight=\"medium\">Native realization</text>\n      <caption>Shared bases, sparse exceptions, native C/Wasm, RepresentationManifold</caption>\n    </grid-item>\n    <grid-item>\n      <text weight=\"medium\">Experiences & distribution</text>\n      <caption>ServiceSite, Matrix, CMS, live pages, demos, GitHub and previews</caption>\n    </grid-item>\n  </grid>\n</box>\n\nThere are useful external quality bars here. <Entity category=\"brand\" value=\"Riverside\" disambig=\"online recording and editing platform\"/> already demonstrates transcript-based editing, visual timelines, scenes and exports; <Entity category=\"brand\" value=\"SAP Signavio\" disambig=\"enterprise process intelligence software\"/> distinguishes event-level process mining from task-level work; and <Entity category=\"brand\" value=\"Granicus\" disambig=\"government meeting and civic engagement software\"/> exposes meeting archives linking agendas, transcripts and video. Merely showing those features as separate cards would be a weak demo—we need to show their connected operational consequence. <Cite refs={[\"turn888860search0\",\"turn888860search1\",\"turn888860search5\"]}/>\n\n### Recommended implementation order\n\nThe biggest shared leverage is to complete five experience foundations before expanding every vertical simultaneously:\n\n| Priority | Experience | Why |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | **#22 ForeignTwin Import & Clip Studio** | Feeds media, civic, research, supplier, property and customer workflows |\n| 2 | **#17 Brief Studio + #21 Verification Network** | Converts discovered opportunities into recipient-specific decisions and executable verification work |\n| 3 | **#27 Frappe Enterprise Workbench** | Makes cross-application business operations visible and actionable using native owners |\n| 4 | **#23 Dallas Civic Media Studio** | Gives us a grounded public source → identity join → playback → work → publication demonstration |\n| 5 | **#05 Creator Audio + #09 Podcast Plant** | Connects the existing native media performance work to polished, user-editable outputs |\n\nThe existing homepage already has an authored **preview reel**. It should remain the leading showcase, followed by the larger catalogue grouped by business outcome. As programs mature, their cards should lead into real workflows, and the corresponding GitHub/source pages, live applications, machine-facing interfaces and guides should point to that same experience—not introduce separate truth.\n\n## Documentation maintenance is now separate and recurring\n\nI set up **weekly Aurekai Guide Maintenance** for Monday mornings, starting October 19.
